theme: Field-level novelty and publication readiness of the project's research contributions
question: Which of the eight candidate contribution families are new at a defensible level and supported strongly enough for publication?
outcome: Two existing scientific cores support focused papers: complete Sanskrit-key calibration and conditional reference laws. Object/source reconciliation is a strong data-paper candidate after a bounded accuracy and release audit. Restoration requires refitting with corrected dependencies; segmentation requires source adjudication and transfer validation. Chronology and rebus studies have named scientific repairs. Earlier primary literature and a pinned October 1 public project preclude several broad novelty claims. A saved-input segmentation replay exactly reproduces the source endpoint.
challenge: Broad themes overlap with prior literature. A mutable public project page could not establish the date of each result. Some book-length sources and full-text routes were unavailable, and this review cannot establish exhaustive priority.
remedy: Compared specific contribution statements with primary passages and public records, inspected a historical GitHub file at commit 1c73645947deba694cb82d42dba967319e8df5a5, separated novelty from evidential strength, recorded scope and source access, and replayed the saved segmentation scorer without opening fresh material.
retry_when: Reassess after the named source adjudications, corrected restoration refit, Tamil matching/parser repairs, or full access to the nearest book-length precedents. Later public studies can also change precise priority judgements.
